title: mmt-bench campaign
description: One campaign file under campaigns/ (#8): one question, and the dimensions matrix.py expands into runs. Checked by `mbench validate`.

name.description: The campaign name of results/<date>-<name>/ (default: the file's stem).

question.description: The one question the campaign answers (plan §B1).

mode.description: offline: pcap from a tmpfs mount. Online comes with #13.

quiet_host.description: True when the campaign needs vLLM stopped: the runner prints the stop and restart commands for Luong and never runs them.

perf.description: True to wrap each pass in `perf stat` on the cell's cores (cycles and instructions per packet, #10). A pass records an unavailable marker — never a fake number — where perf is refused.

tools.description: Adapter names (mmt-probe; Suricata and Snort 3 come with P5).

anyOf.description: A ruleset id: rulesets/<id>/ or rulesets/<id>.so.
A ruleset by id and path: the .so file or the directory holding it, relative to the working directory or absolute.

config_profiles.description: Default: [recommended]. The fair-comparison rule wants both.

oneOf.description: A pcap file pinned by its sha256, with an optional ground-truth file and display name.

threads.description: The tool's thread count (mmt-probe: thread-nb; 0 = the capture thread does the work).

cpusets.description: cpulists the tool's threads are pinned to ("" = unpinned); `core:<fragment>` selects every cpu of the one core type whose model name contains the fragment, resolved from lscpu at run time so no host CPU numbers are committed. The core type is recorded in each run.

repeats.description: Measured passes per matrix cell (methodology: 5), after one warm-up pass.

timeout_s.description: Per-pass cap in seconds; an exceeded pass is killed and recorded as timeout.
